knownGaps: pantheon-ops cannot absorb the repaired sensor until a foundation release carries it; this package deliberately does not bump VERSION, does not write CHANGELOG or release notes, and does not cut or publish a release, because a tag and its release assets cannot be recalled. Release timing is a maintainer decision (manifest humanGates).

ops' existing workaround (seed constants declared inside a `const ( … )` block, e.g. serviceModuleKey) is not rolled back here. Both declaration shapes are now collected, so the workaround stays legal and simply stops being necessary; whether to normalize it is the consumer repository's own review.

The sensor is still a regex-over-source parser, not a Go AST consumer: a constant declared with an initializer that is not a plain quoted string (iota, fmt.Sprintf, a cross-package qualified constant) remains unresolvable. The difference after this change is that such a reference now produces a named finding instead of an empty value, which is the fail-loud half of the fix.
The six uncommitted i18n files in the working tree are not staged, verified or endorsed by this package; check:harness-adoption's two remaining findings belong to them.
Local check:shared-drift and the ops-side matrices were not run: no consumer file is touched from base, and per the Base-first rule the repair reaches ops only through a release.
